items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-20,
notes: Major Transit Station Areas, City of Waterloo

Douglas Stewart gave a presentation outlining the changes to the Zoning By-law as well as the rationale for the changes. He then responded to questions of Council. Adam Lauder, Joel Cotter and Michelle Lee also responded to questions of Council.
Paul Leveck, Urban Legend Developments, Resident of Woolwich spoke in support of staff’s recommendations and offered additional context for the market. He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: New Business
notes: Marijana Saric, Operations, Schooner Street Brewery Inc. – By the Glass Application

Councillor Hanmer spoke about the tournament that the University of Waterloo Women’s Hockey Team, the Waterloo Warriors, is hosting. The 2025 Miller Waste Systems U SPORTS Women's Hockey Championship is at the Woolwich Memorial Centre from March 20-23, 2025. It’s a great opportunity for the Waterloo Warriors to host, playing against teams from across the country.

Councillor Wright shared that the Waterloo Collegiate Institute Orchestra was in New York City last week competing in the National High School Orchestra Cup at the Lincoln Center. They qualified last year when they competed at the MusicFest Canada Nationals, which they won. While they didn’t win the National High School Orchestra Cup, their soloists did. She gave a shout-out to Mr. Piche, the head of the music department at Waterloo Collegiate Institute for the tremendous amount of leadership he has provided over the years.

Councillor Roe attended the Team DAVE, St. David Catholic Secondary School’s robot unveiling for their new robot Suzuki on Friday, February 28. They have created a reef game on YouTube with the robot where you collect large pieces of coral. They’re amazing kids, and she gave a shout-out to them.
Mayor McCabe mentioned that March 8 is International Women’s Day. There are lots of events going on in the Region, including a Women’s Day breakfast hosted by the Chamber of Commerce KW.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve IPPW2025-017. 2. That Council approve the non-routine partial capital funding release for the road reconstruction portion including related underground infrastructure of the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Reconstruction project, funded $1,000,000 from the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund and up to $22,600,000 (current projection) from Development Charges - Debenture, and acknowledge further funding contributions in the amount of $4,600,000 (current projection) from Developer Contributions and $2,100,000 (current projection) from Region of Waterloo Contributions, for total partial funding of $30,300,000, as per the 2024-2026 Approved Capital Budget (Ref. #590). 3. That Council direct staff to proceed with tendering the road reconstruction and related underground infrastructure components of the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Reconstruction project. 4. That Council direct staff to investigate the applicability of the Health and Safety Water Stream (HSWS) grant funding in support of the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Reconstruction project, if this grant stream becomes available. 5. That Council authorize the Commissioner of Integrated Planning & Public Works to execute cost-sharing agreement(s) with the developer group, to address any Developer Contributions for the road reconstruction and related underground infrastructure components of the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Reconstruction Project, subject to such agreement(s) being to the satisfaction of the City’s Director of Engineering Services, and the City Solicitor. 6. That Council direct staff to continue discussions with the developer group regarding a suitable risk-mitigation financing approach for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive Reconstruction project, and report back to Council prior to proceeding with a tender for the pumping station portion of the project.

motions.text: 1. That Council not approve report IPPW2025-014. 2. That Council not approve Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-20, Inclusionary Zoning within Protected Major Transit Stations Areas, City of Waterloo, as set out in Appendix ‘A’ of IPPW2025-014. 3. That Planning staff not be directed to continue to consult with the City of Kitchener, the City of Cambridge, and the Region of Waterloo to evaluate the timing of implementation of Inclusionary Zoning. 4. That Planning staff not be directed to undertake an additional market assessment no later than September 30, 2025. 5. That Planning staff not provide an update to Council no later than November 30, 2025, with the results of the consultation and the market assessment, and to provide recommendations on the timing of implementation of Inclusionary Zoning. And instead: 1. That Council receive report IPPW2025-014. 2. That Council approval Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-20, Inclusionary Zoning within Protected Major Transit Station Areas, with modifications: A. By-law Number 2018-050 is amended by striking out the regulation in Section 3.I.2.c) and replacing it with: Commencing on March 31, 2025, on a LOT that is located within a MAJOR TRANSIT STATION AREA as identified on Schedule ‘A2’ of this BY-LAW, a percentage of GROSS LEASABLE RESIDENTIAL FLOOR AREA shall be set aside for AFFORDABLE DWELLING UNITS in accordance with Table 3C-2, net any rental replacement DWELLING UNIT required under an applicable Rental Replacement By-law, with the following exclusions: i. Development for which a complete Site Plan application is submitted prior to March 31, 2025, pursuant to Section 41 of the PLANNING ACT, provided that a building permit for the development is issued under the BUILDING CODE on or before March 31, 2027. ii. The disposition of lands by the CITY. iii. The disposition of lands by the REGION. B. Section 3.I.2.e) of By-law 2018-050 is amended by deleting the words “by by-law” therein. For the following reasons: • Councillor Bodaly believes that Council should move ahead with Inclusionary Zoning now as there are uncertainties in the market, and market feasibility is not guaranteed • Councillor Bodaly’s alternative motion looks to tackle some of the challenges faced by the development community to offer some flexibility and incentives • Councillor Bodaly looks to address some of the comments received by the development community surrounding fairness and certainty, and moving forward with Inclusionary Zoning, rather than deferring it, would offer that certainty Mayor McCabe left the Chair. (Time: 7:39 p.m.) Councillor Wright in the Chair. (Time: 7:39 p.m.) Mayor McCabe introduced an amendment to Councillor Bodaly’s motion, which replaced the entire motion.
